gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the measured per-channel bitrates side by side. Measured that way, the VIOFO A329S 3CH at maximum bitrate writes about 52 GB an hour across its three cameras (472 + 196 + 196 MB a minute, from Chuck McCoy's DashCamTalk test). The Vantrue N4 Pro S writes about 25 GB an hour (236 + 74 + 107 MB a minute, from EricSan's DashCamTalk test). So the same card holds about twice as many hours of N4 Pro S footage before loop recording overwrites it.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages from Product Bible (2026-11-19), Digital Camera World (2026-10-26), Gearsentials (2026-08-02) and DashCamTalk's best-dash-cams list. None gives a bitrate, a file size or a power draw for any 3-channel camera. Product Bible gives only the makers' temperature ratings, and Gearsentials gives The Hook Up's plate and impact results without figures. Milewitness, which ChatGPT got but did not cite, has part of this: it gives the A329S 3CH figures of 472 and 196 MB a minute and about 52 GB an hour. It has no measured figure for the N4 Pro S or the 70mai T800, so nobody makes the comparison. The cited pages from Car and Driver and VortexRadar returned 403 errors and could not be checked.
decides: This confirms the order in ChatGPT's answer and adds a reason to choose between them. The A329S 3CH spends about twice the bitrate (66 against 32 Mbps on the front camera), which fits its image-quality lead. The Vantrue N4 Pro S records about 25 GB an hour against about 52, so it keeps roughly 10 hours of 3-channel footage on a 256 GB card against about 5. It does this at the lower price, which makes it the honest value pick. The 70mai T800 sits between them at about 35 GB an hour because its rear camera records in 4K. One caveat: the A329S figures were measured at VIOFO's maximum bitrate setting, and VIOFO's FAQ says 15 to 20 hours fit on a 256 GB card at default settings.

findings.label: Average bitrate per channel in 3-channel mode (DashCamTalk review)
findings.value: Front (4K, 30 fps) 32 Mbps; rear (4K, 30 fps) 32 Mbps; cabin (1080p, 30 fps, 4 IR LEDs) 13 Mbps
findings.note: Page published 2026-01-02 with no author named. Sum: 77 Mbps, or 77 / 8 × 3600 / 1000 = about 34.7 GB an hour, which is about 7.4 hours on a 256 GB card. Parking mode is non-buffered and needs the UP03 hardwire kit, or the UP04/UP05 4G kit for cloud features. The maximum microSD card is 512 GB.

findings.label: Bitrate per channel (DashCamTalk spec table)
findings.value: 14.8 Mbps each for front, rear and interior
findings.note: This comes from a spec table, not a measured clip, and the table does not say it applies to 3-channel mode. The same table lists 1440p on all three cameras, while member Hack_man lists 1944p + 1440p + 1440p at 30 fps in 3-channel mode. Sum: 44.4 Mbps, about 20 GB an hour. Treat this as weak data.
